text:
Maria Rivera: Heads-up: CatalystAI (enterprise) is seeing a bunch of 429s starting ~11:02 PDT. Their Token Balance panel in Console shows ~3.4k tokens left for the org. Customer says ~60% of requests in a 90s burst got 429s. Sharing minimal repro below.

Maria Rivera: ```
curl -v -H \"Authorization: Bearer sk-catalystai-prod\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-7b","input":"ping"}' \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate

# got:
# HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
# x-rw-request-id: req_f9e8d7c6
# x-rw-rate-limit-remaining: 0
# x-rw-rate-limit-reset: 1855002000
```

Julian Park: Can you paste the request-id and approximate window? If Console shows tokens, this smells like enforcement (real-time counter) vs reporting disagreement.

Maria Rivera: req_f9e8d7c6. Burst started 11:01:52, peak ~140 req/s for 40s, then intermittent rejects until 11:04.

Samir Patel: Looked into enforcer logs for req_f9e8d7c6 -> enforcer returned 429, reason \"quota_exhausted\", detail: \"atomic-decrement result = -2\". Enforcement is reading/writing to dynamo-quotas (authoritative).

Samir Patel: Reporting path uses telemetry -> kafka -> aggregator -> materialized view -> console. I checked the quota-ingest consumer: ```
# kafka-consumer-groups --describe --group quota-ingest
TOPIC           PARTITION  CURRENT-OFFSET  LOG-END-OFFSET  LAG
quota-events     1          2123340         2123340         0
quota-events     2          2122099         2122389         290
```
partition 2 had ~290 lag around the timeframe.

Kevin Zhou: Also found an SDK telemetry shim bug on the customer's fleet: their client machines had a ~+6s clock skew (ahead). Telemetry events were stamped into the future. Our aggregator bins by event_ts; if ts > now it buffers until the relevant window completes, making Console appear to show more tokens than actually available for ~20-90s.

Julian Park: So enforcement decrements are immediate, while dashboard depends on event timestamps. Future-stamped telemetry delays consumption from showing up -> dashboard overstates available tokens during bursts.

Maria Rivera: Matches what customer reported: immediate 429 responses but Console still looked healthy for ~30-60s, causing confusion.

Samir Patel: Quick local repro I ran:
1) set client clock +6s
2) fire a 100-request burst in 45s
3) watch enforcer counters drop and return 429s
4) Console's token-balance stayed high until future-stamped telemetry was processed

Samir Patel: Minimal telemetry post to emulate: ```
curl -X POST https://telemetry.internal/v1/ingest \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"org":"catalystai","tokens_used":720,"event_ts":"2026-05-14T18:01:58.000Z"}'
```

Kevin Zhou: Short term mitigations: 1) scale quota-ingest consumer parallelism so partition lag goes to 0; 2) add console guardrail: if consumer lag > 30s or >5% of events are future-ts, show a yellow \"metrics delayed\" flag and avoid optimistic token counts.

Julian Park: Long term: 1) normalize timestamps on ingest to server_receive_ts (clamp future_ts to now+1s), 2) alerting when >0.1% events have ts > receive_ts+2s, 3) an offline reconciliation job to compare dynamo quotas vs materialized view weekly and surface diffs per-org.

Maria Rivera: I'll draft the customer note acknowledging the root cause (client clock skew + ingest lag), confirming enforcement is correct, and offering a reconciliation report + one-off credits. Can someone own the reconciliation run for CatalystAI?

Samir Patel: I'll spin up a one-off reconciliation for their org and open a ticket to add consumer-lag alerts. Patched consumer group scaling as P0 for the ingest team.

Kevin Zhou: Opened quick console PR to show the delayed-metrics badge: https://git.redwood.internal/p/console/!2001 and telemetry normalization PR: https://git.redwood.internal/p/telemetry/!2002. Added unit tests for clamping future ts.

Julian Park: Solid. Maria, send the interim message: enforcement is authoritative (their traffic was actually hitting the quota), we're running a reconciliation and will follow up with findings + credits. Also advise customer to check client clock sync and bump to NTP if possible. :white_check_mark:

Maria Rivera: Sending now. Thanks team :raised_hands:
